chunks: Safwan narrated from Yahya al-Azraq who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah, running three or four circuits, and the truthful one (or a reliable companion) meets him and invites him to fulfill a need or to eat. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he answers him, there is no harm, but I prefer that he fulfills the right of God rather than fulfilling the need of his companion.'

key_terms.الصَّدُوق: The truthful one, often referring to a reliable companion or the Imam himself in context
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: Safa and Marwah, the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.حَاجَةَ صَاحِبِهِ: The need of his companion, referring to social or personal obligations
key_terms.حَقَّ اللَّهِ: The right of God, referring to the ritual obligation

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred action for a pilgrim during Sa'i if invited to eat or attend to a need?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of obligations during Sa'i, distinguishing between the ritual duty of Sa'i (Haqq Allah) and social courtesy (Hajat Sahibihi). While answering a companion's call is permissible and not blameworthy, the Imam emphasizes that fulfilling the divine right of the ritual takes precedence, reflecting the Shia scholarly principle of prioritizing core worship over secondary social interactions when time is limited.
